name: Shelumiel
title: Leader of the tribe of Simeon
summary: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, was the chosen leader of the tribe of Simeon during Israel's wilderness journey. He was appointed by God to assist Moses in the census and represented his tribe at the dedication of the tabernacle. He is one of the twelve tribal princes who played a vital role in organizing the people of Israel after their exodus from Egypt.
relatedPersons: Netanel son of Zuar, leader of the tribe of Issachar

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Leader of the Tribe of Simeon
keyEvents.description: God appointed Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, as leader of the tribe of Simeon to assist Moses in the census in the wilderness of Sinai.

keyEvents.title: The Census of the Tribe of Simeon
keyEvents.description: Under Shelumiel's leadership, the men of the tribe of Simeon were counted, totaling 59,300 fighting men aged twenty years and older.

keyEvents.title: Camp Arrangement for the Tribe of Simeon
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Simeon, under Shelumiel's leadership, was positioned next to the camp of Reuben on the south side of the tabernacle.

keyEvents.title: Offering at the Dedication of the Altar
keyEvents.description: On the second day of the dedication of the tabernacle, Shelumiel presented his offering, which included a silver plate, a silver basin, a gold spoon with incense, as well as burnt offerings and sin offerings.

keyEvents.title: Leader During the Departure from Sinai
keyEvents.description: When the people of Israel broke camp from the wilderness of Sinai, Shelumiel led the military division of the tribe of Simeon as part of the organized march.
